panels.text: In June 2018, OpenAI researcher Alec Radford published GPT-1: the Transformer's decoder trained to predict the next word. 117 million parameters, 12 layers, trained on ~7,000 books. It worked well. Not spectacularly. But enough to ask: what if the only limit was scale?

panels.prompt: A dramatic split scene: on the left a researcher quietly releasing a paper with a small shrug, calm and understated atmosphere, on the right the same scene but erupting into chaos with swirling newspaper headlines, camera flashes, social media icons, reporters crowding around, a large bold stamp or seal reading 'TOO DANGEROUS' in red, the contrast between quiet and explosive. NO OTHER TEXT besides TOO DANGEROUS — no dates, no model names, no fine print. Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, calm grey tones on left transitioning to bright red and blue #4A9BD9 energy on right

panels.text: In February 2019, GPT-2 arrived: 1.5 billion parameters, 48 layers. Ten times larger. Then OpenAI announced it was withholding the full model due to misuse concerns. Critics called it publicity-seeking. Supporters called it responsible foresight. Either way, the public was paying attention to language AI for the first time.

A white speech bubble with black outline near the top. Inside the bubble the text reads: "GPT-3 did tasks it was never trained for!" panels.caption: Each generation was roughly 10x larger -- and each unlocked qualitatively new abilities.

panels.text: Scaling revealed a strange law: make a model 10x bigger, and it does not just get 10% better. It sometimes learns entirely new skills the smaller version could not do at all. Nobody programmed these abilities in. They emerged from sheer scale.

GPT-3 was trained only to predict the next word. Yet it learned grammar, facts, translation, coding, and reasoning. Is "predict the next word" really a simple task? Or is it secretly the hardest task there is -- because to predict perfectly, you would need to understand everything?

A white speech bubble with black outline above. Inside the bubble the text reads: "More data plus more compute equals emergent abilities." panels.speaker: SCALEBOT

panels.text: Scaling was working. But raw next-word prediction had a problem: the model would generate toxic content, fabricate facts, and follow harmful instructions. Someone needed to teach it values.
